bugs.title: Double-checkout race condition creates phantom orders and enables money duplication
bugs.description: Concurrent POST /api/orders requests both succeed when cart has items. Two orders are created but balance is only deducted once and stock only decremented once. Returning both orders yields a net profit for the user — balance exceeds original $100 and stock inflates above original levels.
bugs.impact: Financial: users can duplicate money. Inventory: stock integrity violated. Exploitable by any authenticated user.
bugs.reproduction: 1. Login, add book to cart. 2. Fire 2+ concurrent POST /api/orders. 3. Both return 200 with different order IDs. 4. Balance only decremented once. 5. Return both orders → balance > $100.
bugs.rootCause: OrderService.checkout() has no concurrency control — no optimistic locking, no synchronized block, no database-level atomic operation. Multiple threads read the same cart state before any clears it.
bugs.fix: Add @Version field to CartItem/Order for optimistic locking, or use MongoDB transactions, or implement a distributed lock on checkout per userId.
bugs.testName: @bug race: concurrent checkout duplicates order and corrupts balance

bugs.title: Double-return race condition issues multiple refunds for single order
bugs.description: Concurrent POST /api/orders/{id}/return requests on the same order succeed multiple times. The isReturnEligible() check passes for all concurrent requests before any updates the status to RETURNED. Each successful return refunds the full order amount and restores stock.
bugs.impact: Financial: unlimited money generation. Inventory: stock inflation. Exploitable by any authenticated user with a recent order.
bugs.reproduction: 1. Login, purchase a book. 2. Fire 5+ concurrent POST /api/orders/{id}/return. 3. Multiple requests return 200. 4. Balance exceeds original amount. 5. Stock exceeds original count.
bugs.rootCause: OrderService.returnOrder() reads order status and checks isReturnEligible() non-atomically. Race window between status check and status update allows multiple refunds.
bugs.fix: Use MongoDB findAndModify with status check (atomic update) or optimistic locking with @Version.
bugs.testName: @bug race: concurrent returns on same order refund multiple times

bugs.title: Double-buy marketplace race creates multiple orders from single listing
bugs.description: Concurrent POST /api/marketplace/listings/{id}/buy requests all succeed. Multiple orders are created, buyer is charged multiple times, and seller receives multiple payments — all from a single listing that should only be sold once.
bugs.impact: Financial: buyer overcharged, seller overpaid. Data integrity: phantom orders with no corresponding listing. Exploitable by any pair of users.
bugs.reproduction: 1. User1 creates listing at $5.99. 2. User2 fires 5 concurrent buy requests. 3. Multiple succeed (typically 2-5). 4. Buyer charged N × $5.99. 5. Seller receives N × $5.99.
bugs.rootCause: MarketplaceService.buyListing() checks listing status ACTIVE non-atomically. Multiple threads all see ACTIVE before any sets it to SOLD.
bugs.fix: Use MongoDB findOneAndUpdate with {status: 'ACTIVE'} filter to atomically claim the listing.
bugs.testName: @bug race: concurrent buy on same listing creates multiple orders

bugs.title: Concurrent add-to-cart bypasses deduplication creating duplicate entries
bugs.description: Concurrent POST /api/cart/items for the same bookId creates multiple separate cart entries instead of consolidating into a single entry with accumulated quantity. At checkout, each duplicate entry is processed separately — the user is charged for all duplicates but stock is only decremented once per bookId.
bugs.impact: Financial: user charged correctly but stock undercount leads to overselling. Inventory: sold items not fully deducted from stock.
bugs.reproduction: 1. Login. 2. Fire 2+ concurrent POST /api/cart/items with same bookId and qty=1. 3. Cart shows 2+ separate entries for same bookId. 4. Checkout charges for all entries but stock only decremented once.
bugs.rootCause: CartService.addItem() checks for existing cart item by bookId then either updates or inserts. The check-then-act is non-atomic, so concurrent requests both see 'not found' and both insert.
bugs.fix: Use MongoDB upsert with {userId, bookId} as the filter, or use unique compound index on (userId, bookId).
bugs.testName: @bug race: concurrent add-to-cart same book creates duplicate entries

bugs.title: Sidebar balance not updated after checkout
bugs.description: After successful checkout, the sidebar balance display continues showing the pre-checkout amount ($100.00) instead of the updated balance. The correct value only appears after a full page reload.
bugs.impact: UX: user sees incorrect balance, may attempt purchases they cannot afford. No financial impact (server-side balance is correct).
bugs.reproduction: 1. Login (balance $100). 2. Add book ($12.99) to cart. 3. Checkout. 4. Sidebar still shows $100.00. 5. Reload page → shows $87.01.
bugs.rootCause: CartPage.jsx handleCheckout() navigates to order page after checkout but does not call refreshUser() or any mechanism to update the sidebar balance. The AuthContext user object retains the stale balance.
bugs.fix: Call refreshUser() from AuthContext after successful checkout, or update the user state locally after the checkout API response.
bugs.testName: @bug stale-ui: sidebar balance shows stale value after checkout

bugs.title: Cart badge not cleared after checkout
bugs.description: After successful checkout, the cart badge in the sidebar still shows the pre-checkout item count (e.g., '1') even though the cart is now empty server-side. The badge only disappears after a page reload.
bugs.impact: UX: user sees stale cart count, may think items are still in cart.
bugs.reproduction: 1. Login, add item to cart (badge shows '1'). 2. Checkout. 3. Badge still shows '1'. 4. Reload → badge disappears.
bugs.rootCause: Checkout does not trigger a cart state refresh. The CartContext items array is not cleared after checkout.
bugs.fix: Call clearCart() or fetchCart() from CartContext after successful checkout to reset the cart state.
bugs.testName: @bug stale-ui: cart badge persists after checkout

bugs.title: Cart badge not shown after re-login despite server-side cart items
bugs.description: After logout and re-login, the cart badge does not appear on the home page even though the user has items in their server-side cart. The badge only appears after navigating to a page that triggers a cart fetch.
bugs.impact: UX: user doesn't know they have items in cart after logging back in.
bugs.reproduction: 1. Login, add item to cart (badge shows '1'). 2. Logout. 3. Login again. 4. Badge is absent. 5. Navigate to /cart → items are there.
bugs.rootCause: Login flow does not fetch cart data. The CartContext initializes with empty items and only fetches on cart-related page visits or add-to-cart actions.
bugs.fix: Call fetchCart() after successful login to initialize the cart badge.
bugs.testName: @bug stale-ui: cart badge absent on home page after re-login despite server-side cart

bugs.title: Checkout failure silently swallowed — no error feedback to user
bugs.description: When checkout fails (insufficient balance, out of stock, network error), the CartPage shows zero visual feedback. The Checkout button returns to idle state and the user has no idea why the purchase didn't complete.
bugs.impact: UX: user cannot understand why checkout failed. May repeatedly click with no result. Error only visible in browser console.
bugs.reproduction: 1. Login as user with $0 balance. 2. Add book to cart. 3. Click Checkout. 4. Button shows 'Processing...' then returns to 'Checkout'. 5. No error message anywhere on page.
bugs.rootCause: CartPage.jsx handleCheckout() has try/finally but no catch block. API errors are thrown as unhandled AxiosErrors.
bugs.fix: Add catch block to handleCheckout() that sets an error state, displayed as a user-visible message (e.g., 'Insufficient balance' or 'Checkout failed').
bugs.testName: @bug silent-error: insufficient balance checkout shows no error to user

bugs.title: Marketplace buy failure silently swallowed — no error feedback
bugs.description: When buying a marketplace listing fails (insufficient balance, listing already sold), the ListingCard shows no error. The Buy button returns to idle state silently.
bugs.impact: UX: user cannot understand why marketplace purchase failed.
bugs.reproduction: 1. Login as user with $0 balance. 2. Navigate to marketplace. 3. Click Buy on a listing. 4. Button shows 'Buying...' then returns to 'Buy'. 5. No error message.
bugs.rootCause: ListingCard.jsx handleBuy() has try/finally but no catch block.
bugs.fix: Add catch block with error state display on the listing card.
bugs.testName: @bug silent-error: marketplace buy with insufficient balance shows no error

bugs.title: Order return failure silently swallowed — no error feedback
bugs.description: When returning an order fails (API error, network issue), the OrderDetailPage shows no error. The Return Order button returns to idle state silently.
bugs.impact: UX: user cannot understand why return failed. Lower severity since return failures are less common.
bugs.reproduction: 1. Login, view a completed order. 2. Intercept return API to simulate error. 3. Click Return Order. 4. Button shows 'Returning...' then returns to 'Return Order'. 5. No error message.
bugs.rootCause: OrderDetailPage.jsx handleReturn() has try/finally but no catch block.
bugs.fix: Add catch block with error state display on the order detail page.
bugs.testName: @bug silent-error: return order with API error shows no feedback

bugs.title: No 404 page — unknown routes render blank main content area
bugs.description: Navigating to any undefined route (e.g., /nonexistent, /admin/settings) renders the sidebar but a completely blank main content area. No 'Page not found' message, no navigation hints.
bugs.impact: UX: confused user sees a blank page. Sidebar still provides navigation recovery.
bugs.reproduction: 1. Navigate to http://localhost:7547/nonexistent-route. 2. Main area is empty. 3. No '404' or 'Page not found' text.
bugs.rootCause: App.jsx has no catch-all <Route path='*'> element. Unmatched routes render no component in the <Routes> outlet.
bugs.fix: Add <Route path='*' element={<NotFoundPage />} /> to App.jsx with a user-friendly 404 page.
bugs.testName: @bug ui-ux: unknown route renders blank main area with no guidance

bugs.title: Search input not synced with URL query parameter
bugs.description: When navigating directly to /?query=Dune, the search results are displayed correctly but the search input field is empty. The SearchBar component uses local useState('') and does not read from URL params.
bugs.impact: UX: user sharing a search URL or using browser back/forward sees results but an empty search box — confusing.
bugs.reproduction: 1. Navigate to /?query=Dune. 2. Books matching 'Dune' are shown. 3. Search input is empty (should show 'Dune').
bugs.rootCause: SearchBar.jsx initializes search state with useState('') and never reads from searchParams. The component is uncontrolled relative to the URL.
bugs.fix: Initialize SearchBar state from useSearchParams().get('query') and update it when URL changes.
bugs.testName: @bug ui-ux: navigating to search URL shows results but search input is empty

bugs.title: Wrong error message for returning already-returned orders
bugs.description: When attempting to return an order that was already returned, the API responds with 'Return window has expired' instead of a more accurate message like 'Order already returned'.
bugs.impact: UX: misleading error message. User thinks the time window expired when the real issue is the order was already processed.
bugs.reproduction: 1. Purchase and return an order. 2. Attempt to return the same order again. 3. Error message: 'Return window has expired' (incorrect — should mention order already returned).
bugs.rootCause: OrderService.returnOrder() uses isReturnEligible() which checks both status === COMPLETED AND time window. When status is RETURNED, isReturnEligible() returns false, but the error message always blames the time window.
bugs.fix: Add separate status check: if order.status === 'RETURNED', throw 'Order already returned'. Only check time window for COMPLETED orders.
bugs.testName: @bug ui-ux: returning already-returned order shows 'Return window expired' instead of 'Already returned'

bugs.title: Floating point precision artifacts in balance after marketplace transactions
bugs.description: After multiple marketplace buy/sell transactions, user balances display floating point noise (e.g., $82.03000000000002 instead of $82.03, or $117.96999999999998 instead of $117.97).
bugs.impact: UX: confusing balance display. No financial impact since the difference is sub-cent.
bugs.reproduction: 1. User1 creates 3 listings at $5.99 each. 2. User2 buys all 3. 3. User2 balance: 82.03000000000002 (should be 82.03). 4. User1 balance: 117.96999999999998 (should be 117.97).
bugs.rootCause: Java double type used for monetary calculations. IEEE 754 floating point cannot represent $5.99 exactly, and repeated additions accumulate error.
bugs.fix: Use BigDecimal for all monetary fields and calculations, or store amounts in cents as integers.
bugs.testName: @bug ui-ux: repeated marketplace transactions cause floating point artifacts in balance
